messages.subject: Line number via Highlight
parts:
Hi,

I'd like to use the highlight line_number option for adding line
numbers to my cdoe appendix.

In particular, it would be wonderful if line numbers would be
running.

To make it clear imagine the following appendix

\appendix
Regressions in table \vref{tab:q2} are generated with the following
code:
<<sc1, ref.label ='q2-reg'>>=
@

Table \vref{tab:sigma} is generated as:
<<sc2, ref.label = 'q2-other-reg'>>=
@

I would like to number sc1 with 1,5,10,...,n and then let sc2 start
with <first j so n + j %% 5 == 0>, j + 5,...
and so forth.

Would that be possible?

Thanks in advance,
Rasmus

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Line number via Highlight
parts:
Hi,

I believe you are talking about Romain's highlight package, and I have
bugged him for a few times but the new version is still not on CRAN,
so I cannot really support it. I do not know if it is possible for the
highlight package either, but I think the LaTeX package listings
should be able to do this. You just need to go to the listings manual
and find out the appropriate options, then set up output hooks in
knitr; see http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/listings/ for example.

Regards,

I had coded up a "hack" long back (https://github.com/yihui/knitr/commit/6baa70dcc9ccb662b74609d6f5bcaa835fe561ea) that inserts the line numbers into the tex file after `knitr` has processed the rnw to tex. It should work for your case. 

You will see in the same link that there is a modified `knit2pdf` function that automatically does the insertion for you.

Hopefully, once the `highlight` package implements this functionality, such hacks won't be required.

Best,
Ramnath

> processed
> the rnw to tex. It should work for your case.

I extended the hack a bit, mostly on the tex side. Line numbers are
c(1, 5, 10, ...)

and they are placed in the margin as oppose to the code area (similar to
listings). In theory, one should easily be able to modify the knit
script to allow for specifying how often to insert a number

$ cat myknit
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

local({

insert_line_numbers <- function(tex_file, By = 5){
require(stringr)
doc <- readLines(tex_file)
code_lines <- grep("^(\\\\hlstd|\\\\hlfunctioncall)", doc)
max_lines <- length(code_lines)
line_numbers <- rep('', max_lines)
line_numbers[c(1, seq(5, max_lines, by=By))] <- c('1', seq(5, max_lines, by=By))
line_numbers <- str_pad(line_numbers, nchar(line_numbers[max_lines])+1)
## line_numbers <- str_pad(seq_along(code_lines), width = 2, side = "left")
## line_numbers <- str_c("\\1\\\\hlline\\{", line_numbers, " \\}\\2")
line_numbers <- str_c("\\\\hlline\\{\\\\llap\\{", line_numbers, " \\\\quad\\}\\}\\1\\2")

pat <- "^(\\\\hlstd\\{\\}|\\\\hlfunctioncall\\{.*\\})(.*)$"
doc[code_lines] <- str_replace(doc[code_lines], pat, line_numbers)
writeLines(doc, tex_file)
## return(path.expand(tex_file))
}


p = commandArgs(TRUE)
if (length(p) == 0L || '--help' %in% p) {
message('usage:
knit input [output] [--pdf]
knit --help to print help messages')
q()
}

library(knitr)
knit_fun = if ('--pdf' %in% p) {
p = setdiff(p, '--pdf')
if (length(p) == 0L) stop('no input file provided')
knit2pdf
} else knit

if (!file.exists(p[1]))
stop("file '", p[1], "' does not exist!")

lineno <- FALSE
if ('--lineno' %in% p) {
lineno <- TRUE
p = setdiff(p, '--lineno')
}

knit_fun(p[1], if (length(p) < 2L) NULL else p[2])
if(lineno) {insert_line_numbers(gsub('Rnw$', 'tex', p[1]))}

})
